steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Representation in film refers to the ways in which different social groups, identities and experiences are constructed, depicted and made meaningful on screen.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Gender representation in Hollywood has historically prioritised male protagonists and marginalised female characters into limited roles such as the damsel, the love interest or the mother figure.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Bechdel Test highlights the minimal representation of women in film by asking whether a film features two named women who talk to each other about something other than a man.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Laura Mulvey's concept of the male gaze argues that Hollywood cinema positions women as objects of visual pleasure for a presumed heterosexual male viewer, fragmenting the female body through camera work.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link representation to specific film examples and analyse how meaning is constructed through film language choices. Use theoretical frameworks — Mulvey, intersectionality, stereotype theory — to give your analysis depth and precision. Consider both what is represented and what is absent — omission is itself a representational choice. Discuss how representation reflects and reinforces or challenges dominant ideological positions in society. Acknowledge complexity: most films both challenge and reinforce stereotypes in different ways simultaneously.
